# StreamPay error surface

Every expected failure is a `StreamError` with a stable numeric code. This document is generated from the contract's instrumentation (`src/surface.rs`): each row is a *branch* — one `(entrypoint, condition)` validation decision — mapped to the code it returns. The `error_surface_test.rs` matrix proves every reachable branch fires its code and every code is produced (or retired).

## Error codes

| Code | Variant | Status | Processed by | Meaning |
| ---: | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `StreamNotFound` | reachable (1 branch(es)) | `available`, `cancel_stream`, `get_stream`, `top_up`, `withdraw`, `withdraw_max` | no stream is stored under the id |
| 2 | `NotStreamSender` | **retired** (unreachable) | — | Reserved role check from the original draft. The contract authorizes sender-only actions by comparing the caller address directly and uses `NotAuthorized` (#12) otherwise, so this variant is never returned. Retained for wire compatibility. |
| 3 | `NotStreamRecipient` | **retired** (unreachable) | — | Reserved role check from the original draft. Recipient-only actions require the recipient's authorization (`require_auth`) and use `NotAuthorized` (#12) for business-rule rejections, so this variant is never returned. Retained for wire compatibility. |
| 4 | `StreamNotCancellable` | reachable (1 branch(es)) | `cancel_stream` | the recipient calls cancel_stream on a stream created non-cancelable |
| 5 | `StreamNotActive` | reachable (1 branch(es)) | `cancel_stream`, `top_up`, `withdraw`, `withdraw_max` | the stream status is Cancelled or Depleted |
| 6 | `StartTimeInPast` | reachable (2 branch(es)) | `authorize_agent`, `create_stream` | start_time is before the current ledger timestamp; expires_at is before or equal to current ledger timestamp |
| 7 | `InvalidTimeRange` | reachable (2 branch(es)) | `authorize_agent`, `create_stream` | end_time is not strictly after start_time (zero or negative duration); period_duration is zero |
| 8 | `DurationTooLong` | reachable (1 branch(es)) | `create_stream` | duration exceeds MAX_DURATION_SECONDS (100 years) |
| 9 | `ZeroAmount` | reachable (6 branch(es)) | `authorize_agent`, `create_stream`, `top_up`, `withdraw`, `withdraw_treasury` | deposit_amount is zero or negative; withdraw amount is zero or negative; top-up amount is zero or negative; treasury withdrawal amount is zero or negative; max_per_period is zero or negative; max_per_stream is zero or negative |
| 10 | `AmountExceedsAvailable` | reachable (1 branch(es)) | `withdraw` | amount exceeds the accrued-but-unwithdrawn balance |
| 11 | `MathOverflow` | reachable (6 branch(es)) | `available`, `cancel_stream`, `create_stream`, `streamed_at`, `top_up`, `withdraw`, `withdraw_max` | deposit + amount would overflow i128; deposit * duration would overflow u128; deposit * elapsed would overflow u128; withdrawn exceeds streamed (an invariant-violating stored stream); the cancel pro-rata split would underflow; withdrawn + amount would overflow i128 |
| 12 | `NotAuthorized` | reachable (2 branch(es)) | `cancel_stream`, `revoke_agent` | the caller is neither the sender nor the recipient; caller revoking agent is not the stream recipient |
| 13 | `NothingToWithdraw` | reachable (1 branch(es)) | `withdraw_max` | nothing has accrued yet, or everything accrued was already withdrawn |
| 14 | `FeeRateTooHigh` | reachable (1 branch(es)) | `set_fee_bps` | new_fee_bps exceeds MAX_FEE_BPS (the protocol cap) |
| 15 | `NotGovernor` | reachable (2 branch(es)) | `accept_governor`, `nominate_governor`, `set_fee_bps`, `withdraw_treasury` | the caller is not the treasury governor; the caller is not the nominated governor |
| 16 | `NoPendingGovernor` | reachable (1 branch(es)) | `accept_governor` | accept_governor with no nomination pending |
| 17 | `InsufficientTreasuryBalance` | reachable (1 branch(es)) | `withdraw_treasury` | amount exceeds fees collected minus fees already withdrawn |
| 18 | `AgentNotAuthorized` | reachable (1 branch(es)) | `withdraw_delegated` | agent is not authorized or revoked for this stream |
| 19 | `AgentExpired` | reachable (1 branch(es)) | `withdraw_delegated` | agent session key authorization has expired |
| 20 | `CapExceededPeriod` | reachable (1 branch(es)) | `withdraw_delegated` | withdrawal amount exceeds remaining period cap for agent |
| 21 | `CapExceededStream` | reachable (1 branch(es)) | `withdraw_delegated` | withdrawal amount exceeds remaining total stream cap for agent |

## Retired codes

Codes are append-only: a retired code is never renumbered, reused, or removed — its numeric slot is reserved forever so existing clients keep decoding every code they know. The coverage test (`every_error_code_is_produced_or_retired`) exempts exactly the codes below; any *other* code with zero reachable branches fails CI.

| Code | Variant | Why unreachable |
| ---: | --- | --- |
| 2 | `NotStreamSender` | Reserved role check from the original draft. The contract authorizes sender-only actions by comparing the caller address directly and uses `NotAuthorized` (#12) otherwise, so this variant is never returned. Retained for wire compatibility. |
| 3 | `NotStreamRecipient` | Reserved role check from the original draft. Recipient-only actions require the recipient's authorization (`require_auth`) and use `NotAuthorized` (#12) for business-rule rejections, so this variant is never returned. Retained for wire compatibility. |

## Defensive branches

A defensive branch is a `checked_*` guard whose precondition the contract's invariants rule out for any stored stream. It has a code (so it is not a dead *code*) but cannot be triggered; the matrix test asserts it never fires: `AvailableBalanceOverflow`, `CancelSplitOverflow`, `PayoutOverflow`.
